claim: For every integer \(d\ge 2\) and every \(\kappa\ge1\), let \(C\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) be symmetric positive definite, with \(\lambda_{\max}(C)=1\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(C)=1/\kappa\). On the isotropic quadratic \(f(x)=\|x\|_2^2/2\) with known optimum zero, apply one step of the exact LCD3 local-curvature projection using the constant admissible lower-curvature matrix \(C\). Set \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\), \(u_{\kappa}=\min\{\varphi^{-1},\sqrt{1-1/\kappa}\}\), and \(F(u)=u^2(1-u)/(1+u)\). Then the *sharp*, dimension-independent one-step objective amplification is \(\sup_{x\ne0}f(x^+)/f(x)=\kappa F(u_{\kappa})\), and a maximizer always lies in the sum of the extreme eigenspaces of \(C\). For \(\kappa\ge\varphi\), this equals \((5\sqrt5-11)\kappa/2\). Consequently, the objective is nonincreasing for every initial vector if and only if \(\kappa\le(11+5\sqrt5)/2\). For each larger \(\kappa\), an explicit two-dimensional extreme-eigenvector mixture gives a strict objective increase. This is a one-step classification under a fixed curvature normalization, not an assertion of divergence or failure of LCD3 to converge.

correctness.rationale: C is an admissible lower-curvature mapping because C<=I<=C+(1-1/kappa)I. The exact LCD3 formula gives ratio 1-2 alpha m1+alpha^2 m2 with alpha=1-sqrt(1-1/m1). The spectral chord lambda^2<=(kappa+1)lambda-kappa is exact at endpoints and realizable for every mean; substituting u=sqrt(1-1/m1) gives kappa*u^2*(1-u)/(1+u). Its derivative 2u(1-u-u^2)/(1+u)^2 gives the golden maximizer and exact threshold. Two eigendirections attain equality for each kappa. Reproducible verify.py checks both branches and witnesses, but proof does not depend on finite tests.

value.rationale: Quantifies a motivated algorithmic boundary for the published LCD3 method, whose general stability/convergence theory is absent. Gives a sharp all-dimensional spectral envelope and a necessary-and-sufficient universal one-step monotonicity threshold with explicit extremizers and unbounded objective overshoot even though the objective Hessian is the identity. Shows a structural Euclidean-versus-curvature-metric contrast with LCD2. This is more than a cheap validity check or a manually chosen isolated example.
